$comment: Read by site/src/digests.js for /courses, checked by scripts/digest-check.mjs. 'mine' is James's own courses (facts from JamesLiuZX/udemy course.yaml; set url once a course is live). 'picks' grows with each AI digest run, newest added last; DIGEST.md has the rules. No em dashes.

mine.title: AI Product Skills for PMs & Analysts
mine.promise: Stop guessing whether the AI feature your team ships actually works: eval-based acceptance criteria, a golden-set eval harness, token economics and de-risking hallucination.

mine.title: AI Agents for Your Job
mine.promise: Build agents that triage your inbox, draft your reports and chase your invoices with n8n, then learn to check their work and know what never to automate.

mine.title: AI UGC & Video Ads
mine.promise: Build the creative testing machine: brief, batch-generate statics and UGC video with AI, pre-flight compliance failures and run tests that find winners.

picks.title: AI Agents, CMU 11-768 (Fall 2026)
picks.provider: Carnegie Mellon University, Graham Neubig and Daniel Fried
picks.why: A graduate course on building agent harnesses, designing evals and training agents with RL. Recordings post as the term runs to 3 Dec.

picks.title: Complete Claude Code Course: Beginner to Advanced
picks.why: Covers MCP, skills, subagents, debugging and testing. Badged hot and new, rated 4.6 from 165 reviews, updated October 2026.

picks.title: Claude Code 2026: Agents Teams, Subagents, MCP & Skills
picks.why: A short 2h 35m route through CLAUDE.md, skills, MCP, hooks and scheduling. Updated October 2026.

picks.title: MCP Security Fundamentals
picks.why: About two hours on how AI agents get exploited and how to break the lethal trifecta with architectural boundaries instead of prompt filters. Posted 29 Oct 2026.

picks.title: Learn Vector Databases for Beginners: Embeddings, Similarity Search & ChromaDB
picks.why: A 1.5-hour start on embeddings, cosine similarity and HNSW and IVF indexes, ending with a semantic search build in ChromaDB. Posted 3 Nov 2026.

picks.title: Jev Course: Prefill-Only Inference and Decision Models from Scratch
picks.why: About two hours of PyTorch on models that classify and act in the prefill pass instead of decoding token by token, with KV-cache reuse across repeated system prompts. Posted 29 Oct 2026.

picks.title: Build a Hybrid Search Engine in PostgreSQL: BM25 + Vector Retrieval
picks.why: About an hour on keyword and vector search inside one PostgreSQL database, merged with Reciprocal Rank Fusion in SQL, over 240,000 Simple English Wikipedia articles. Posted 21 Oct 2026.

picks.title: Learn Agentic Coding with Codex & AI Coding Agents
picks.provider: freeCodeCamp.org, taught by Tom Chant of Scrimba
picks.why: About two hours on prompts and AGENTS.md files, Plan Mode and skills, testing agent changes and MCP, with a section on using Git safely with an agent and protecting API keys and other secrets. Posted 10 Nov 2026.

picks.title: The Anatomy of an AI Data Center
picks.why: An 8-hour tour of power, cooling, optical networking and multi-gigawatt construction, ending on the economics of GPU cloud hosting and capacity contracts. Posted 16 Oct 2026.

picks.title: Agentic Payments: How AI Agents Move Money
picks.provider: Maven free lesson by Zdenek Nemec (Superface.ai) and Emmanuel Paraskakis
picks.why: A 60-minute recorded lesson from 23 Sep 2026 that sorts agent payments into commerce, machine payments and treasury, covers ACP, UCP, AP2, x402 and Visa and Mastercard payment identity, and ends with a way to prioritize a payments roadmap.

picks.title: Build and Train a GLM-5.3-Flash Model From Scratch with Python
picks.why: 44 minutes through tokenization, linear and sparse attention, mixture-of-experts routing, image tokens, pre-training experiments and reward design for reinforcement learning. Posted 14 Nov 2026.

picks.title: AI Red Teaming Course: 100 Labs, Attack & Defend LLMs
picks.provider: Udemy (the course page names no instructor)
picks.why: 112 lectures and 8h 35m of labs against a local, deliberately vulnerable sandbox: prompt injection, jailbreaks, RAG poisoning, MCP-based agent exploits, guardrails and PyRIT. Rated 4.7 from only 9 ratings, last updated October 2026.

picks.title: Claude Certified Developer Foundations Course
picks.why: 8 hours on agent architectures, the Claude APIs and SDKs, tool use and MCP servers, context engineering, and defending against prompt injection and data leaks. Prepares for the Claude Certified Developer Foundations exam. Posted 24 Sep 2026.

picks.title: CS 329Z: Engineering AI Agents (Stanford, Fall 2026)
picks.provider: Stanford University, Diyi Yang, Michael Ryan and John Yang
picks.why: Building agents from scratch: foundations, RAG, tool use, frameworks, design patterns, memory, multi-agent systems and optimization across the 9 lecture videos linked so far. The evaluation, LLM-as-judge and agent safety lectures have slides up but no video yet. Assumes an NLP course or equivalent background.

picks.title: CMU AI Agents 2026: 13. Agentic Safety
picks.provider: Carnegie Mellon University, Graham Neubig (a lecture from CMU 11-768)
picks.why: One lecture on making agentic systems safe, from the CMU course picked on 6 Nov, posted 16 Oct 2026. Watch it before you write the allow list for an agent that can use a computer.

picks.title: Learn Real-World Penetration Testing: Hands-On Ethical Hacking Crash Course
picks.why: About 2.5 hours (the link says a 3-hour watch) against a practice Capture The Flag machine: Linux, Nmap reconnaissance, finding hidden directories and endpoints, Burp Suite and scripted recon in Bash and Python. The attacker's side of the inference-host breaches Dragos found. Posted 29 Oct 2026.

picks.title: Governing AI Agents
picks.provider: DeepLearning.AI with Databricks, taught by Amber Roberts
picks.why: A 1h30m beginner course: give an agent its own identity, restrict it to the data it needs with masked views of an HR dataset, and log its inputs, outputs and decisions. Not new (updated 17 Jul 2026), but the closest hands-on match to the controls US banks are adding to their own agents.

picks.title: Stanford CS 329Z, lecture 4: Tool Use & Function Calling
picks.provider: Stanford University, from Engineering AI Agents (Diyi Yang, Michael Ryan and John Yang)
picks.why: One lecture, given on 5 Oct 2026, from the Stanford course picked on 22 Nov: why models need tools, the interfaces from REST to function calling to MCP, and how to evaluate tool use with BFCL, ToolBench and τ-bench. Its MCP reading is the 2025-06-18 spec, so it predates server-shipped skills and the new Tasks extension.

picks.title: OAuth 2.0 Course for Beginners
picks.why: A 2-hour build of an authorization server, a resource server and a client app using the authorization code flow with PKCE. Not new (posted 6 Jan 2026), but scoped, short-lived tokens are one way to give an AI agent a narrow permission instead of a password.
